content.comment_body: Is it possible to use the cursor key on the [product_name] operator panel to activate the relay coil? I tested this in simulation, and it worked, but on the actual hardware it does not function. Thank you for any help.
Hello, If you refer to the manual, you'll find that you need to press both the ESC and cursor key simultaneously. In the simulation, you only need to click once.

In your program, you must set specific parameters for the cursor buttons such as 'Momentary pushbutton (make)' so that the cursors operate correctly in reality. Also, [product_name] engineering software offers an ONLINE TEST feature where you can observe program operation.
I did not check the instructions initially—just experimented and it worked. Thank you for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: A user noticed that the behavior of the cursor key to trigger a relay coil differs between simulation and the physical device. The discrepancy is due to the different input requirements: real hardware needs both ESC and cursor keys pressed together. Consulting documentation and understanding device operation processes help resolve such differences.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that the hardware would work the same way as the simulation, specifically that pressing the cursor key alone would activate the relay coil.
